rationale: The source rejects extending Proposition 2.7.1(c) from 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3 to all |lambda| <= 1/K3. The Lean proposition encodes precisely the counterexample form of that impossibility, and the explicit Dirac/constant-zero choice at K3=1 and lambda=-1 is admissible, finite, and violates the bound because 1 > exp(-1). Both implication directions therefore hold, and the specialization to a real-line probability law is harmless for this existential claim.
